newsitem.title: GERMANY: Softening euro out of question, Waigel says.
newsitem.headline: Softening euro out of question, Waigel says.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Saturday Germany would not tolerate any softening of plans for Europe's single currency, the euro.
"A softeing of the euro is out of the question with us," Waigel told reporters at a conference of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party in the southern town of Trossenfurt.
Waigel said no one would lose a single deutschemark because of economic and monetary union (EMU).

He said every fourth job in Germany wass dependent on export and a negative discussion about the project would simply mean more capital flowed into the mark. Germany would then pay the price with a lack of economic growth, he said.
Earlier on Saturday, Waigel insisted Germany was aiming to meet all the criteria for EMU and was not discussing a delay.
